land.text: Kedah, which Srivijaya held: 'the Buddhist Srivijaya kingdom was in direct control of Kedah'

predecessors.note: The infobox lists 'Kedah Kingdom and Srivijaya' as predecessors; the Srivijaya dossier (se-02-a) records Kedah leaving Srivijaya in 1139, Cliopatria's year.

land.text: the pre-Islamic Hindu-Buddhist kingdom of Kedah, whose ruler Phra Ong Mahawangsa converted to Islam

predecessors.note: No dossier exists for the earlier kingdom ('Kedah Tua', the Bujang Valley); Cliopatria has no row for it.

land.text: Kedah, which 'became a British protectorate in 1909' by the Anglo-Siamese Treaty

successors.note: The sultan stayed on his throne as a protected ruler (infobox 'Protectorate of the United Kingdom (1909-1941; 1945-1946)'); the sultanate continues inside Malaysia, but as a sovereign or tributary state the dossier ends in 1909. Cliopatria ends the row in 1910.

capitals.name: Alor Setar
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Alor Setar Anak Bukit' ('Remains as capital until today'). The page places Durbar Raja II's palace 'at Bukit Meriam in 1136' and dates no move between the two; Alor Setar is drawn for the whole life as the only seat the page names. Siam took Alor Setar in November 1821 and Tengku Kudin briefly retook it in 1831.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but holding from 1136: 'Conversion to Islam: 1136' and 'the Sultanate of Kedah started in 1136 when King Phra Ong Mahawangsa converted to Islam'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria begins in 1139. 13,167 km2, 38 grid cells: Kedah's own 31 cells, Perlis 2, the Seberang Perai coast 2, one cell each in Satun and Songkhla; the page gives no area. The date is the chronicle's: the page also says 'an Acehnese account gives the conversion of Kedah to Islam in 1474', and that Kedah 'may have remained Hindu-Buddhist until the 15th century'.

Unverified: page budget. 18,586 km2: 18 more cells than 1139, all in Satun (8) and Songkhla (11 to 12), a strip no other Cliopatria polity holds in 1294-1458. No page opened mentions Kedah north of Perlis in these centuries; the Kedah Sultanate page says only that 'Thai chronicles mention that Kedah was a Thai city like Nakhon Si Thammarat'. A gap-filler should open the Tambralinga and Sukhothai pages.
Unverified: page budget. Same northern strip as 1294 less one cell (100.1E 7.0N); nothing on the pages changes Kedah's extent in 1375, when Cliopatria's Ayutthaya begins to neighbour it.

Unverified: page budget. Back to the Kedah core (13,312 km2, 38 cells): the 18 northern cells go to Cliopatria's Ayutthaya Kingdom in 1459 (the Ayutthaya dossier, se-01, records the same cells as a 1459 gain and notes its page dates no southern conquest). The Kedah Sultanate page has Kedah in this century as Malacca's vassal ('The request by Kedah was in response to be Malacca's vassal, probably due to fears of Ayutthayan aggression'), undated; that tie is Malacca's to record.
Unverified: page budget. Core of 37 cells (13,083 km2). Malacca fell in 1511; the page says nothing of Kedah's frontier then.
Unverified: page budget. One cell more than 1512 (100.55E 6.51N, on the Perlis side); a single-cell edge effect, not an event of any page.

Unverified: page budget. The same cell drops out again. The page's one dated event in these decades is Aceh's capture of Sultan Sulaiman Shah in 1619 ('Sulaiman Shah, who was captured by Aceh in 1619'), which moved no border.

13,083 km2 to 1799. The shape holds the Seberang Perai coast (2 cells, 100.46E-100.51E) but not Penang Island, which the British took in 1786 ('Light and his entourage sailed on to Penang Island, where they arrived on 17 July 1786'); the island is a ledger event with no effect on this shape. The page gives no area.

correction.text: unchanged for 1800-1807: the Seberang Perai coast is already out ('a treaty came into effect that gave the British sovereignty over Seberang Perai' on 7 July 1800); from 1808 Setul is out as well (keyframe 1808)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1800 shape loses exactly the two Seberang Perai cells of 1799 (11,334 km2), as the 1800 treaty requires. It keeps one Satun cell (Setul) to 1821 although Siam created the Kingdom of Setul Mambang Segara in 1808; the 1808 keyframe removes it. The page gives no area.

correction.text: Kedah without Setul: Siam appointed 'Tunku Bisnu as ruler of Setul, thus establishing the Kingdom of Setul Mambang Segara in 1808'; Setul read as Satun province

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1800 shape minus its single Satun cell. Setul is read as the Satun province (the Perlis page: Monthon Syburi comprised Kedah, Perlis and Satun, '(but Satun remained with Thailand)'); the page describes Setul's territory nowhere. Kedah's 1821 annexation follows.

9,327 km2, 28 of the 33 cells of modern Kedah state. After the Siamese annexation (November 1821) and the 1839 partition, 'In 1842, the Sultan agreed to accept Siamese terms and was restored to the throne of Kedah'; Siam then made Perlis a separate principality, a direct vassal of Bangkok (the page, paraphrased) The shape lacks Perlis, Setul and Kubang Pasu ('another historical Malay Kingdom born during the Partition of Kedah', Kedah Sultanate page) and, on the grid, Langkawi: those five cells sit in Cliopatria's separate Kedah-Perlis District row (se-03), so this shape is Kedah proper. No page opened mentions Langkawi, so that split is unverified. Valid 1842-1891; Setul returns in 1892.

correction.text: Kedah proper with Setul: 'In 1892, the kingdom was reunified with the Kedah Sultanate'; Setul read as Satun province

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page's sentence does not name the kingdom in the text read; it follows the account of Setul Mambang Segara, and the 1909 sentence 'finally ended Kedahan rule over Setul' confirms Kedah held Setul before 1909. The extent of Setul is the Satun province as an assumption.

correction.text: the 1895 shape with Setul (Satun) still held, until the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909 'finally ended Kedahan rule over Setul'

keyframe_review.note: 9,557 km2: one cell (100.62E 5.18N, on the Perak border) more than 1842-1894, a cell Cliopatria gives to Perak (1842-1876) and the British (to 1894); no page opened mentions it. The shape lacks Setul, which the page says Kedah held from 1892 to 1909.

correction.text: the shape with Setul, ending in July 1909, not 1910: 'It was originally an independent state, but became a British protectorate in 1909'; infobox 'Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909: 9 July 1909'

keyframe_review.note: Years and Setul: Cliopatria runs to 1910; the page ends Kedah's independence in July 1909 and the treaty took Setul out of Kedah's jurisdiction the same day. No area on the page to compare with 9,557 km2.

region.text: Kedah; the page names only Durbar Raja II's palace at Bukit Meriam

ledger.note: 1136: Kedah becomes a sultanate when its ruler converts to Islam. 'At-Tarikh Salasilah Negeri Kedah described the conversion to Islam as starting in 1136 AD'; infobox 'Conversion to Islam: 1136'; 'the Sultanate of Kedah was formed when King Phra Ong Mahawangsa converted to Islam'. The page lists Sultan Mudzafar Shah I as first sultan in 1136 but also an Acehnese account of 1474. Cliopatria starts the polity in 1139; the Kedah page also has 'the Sultanate of Kedah started in 1136'.

region.text: the Satun-Songkhla strip Cliopatria adds in 1294 (18 cells)

ledger.note: c. 1294: Kedah's outline grows to Satun and Songkhla (year is Cliopatria's; the page is silent). No other Cliopatria polity holds those cells in 1294-1458, hence 'nobody'; the Kedah Sultanate page says Kedah was under Srivijaya's direct control and, in the Thai chronicles, 'a Thai city like Nakhon Si Thammarat', without years.

1459: the northern strip passes to Ayutthaya in Cliopatria (page silent; the year is Cliopatria's). The Ayutthaya dossier (se-01) records the same cells as a 1459 gain and says its own page dates no southern conquest.

1786: Francis Light takes possession of Penang for the East India Company. 'Light and his entourage sailed on to Penang Island, where they arrived on 17 July 1786', with the formal possession ceremony on 11 August; the agreement included 'a lease of 6,000 Spanish dollars to cancel Kedah's debts to Siam'. The Kedah Sultanate page: 'the Sultan agreed to hand over Penang to the British'. The island is in no Cliopatria Kedah shape.

region.text: Seberang Perai (Province Wellesley), the mainland strip opposite Penang

ledger.note: 1800: Kedah cedes Seberang Perai. 'On 7 July 1800, while George Alexander William Leith was Lieutenant-Governor of Penang, a treaty came into effect that gave the British sovereignty over Seberang Perai', named Province Wellesley. The Penang page: 'gained a 189.3 km2 (73.1 sq mi) strip of Seberang Perai from the new Sultan of Kedah', with the Perai River as the border and the annual payment raised to 10,000 Spanish dollars.

region.text: Setul: Siam appointed 'Tunku Bisnu as ruler of Setul'

ledger.note: 1808: Siam creates the Kingdom of Setul Mambang Segara out of Kedah. 'Sultan Dziaddin was forced to abdicate in 1803 by the King of Siam'; Siam then appointed 'Tunku Bisnu as ruler of Setul, thus establishing the Kingdom of Setul Mambang Segara in 1808.' The Siamese invasion of Kedah page instead has Tunku Bisnu made ruler of Setul in 1811 (reviewer se-02-b). The page describes no boundary; Setul is read as Satun province and only Cliopatria's single Satun cell is removed.

region.text: the whole of Kedah, annexed by Siam

ledger.note: 1821: Siam conquers and annexes Kedah. 'Rama II then ordered Phraya Nakhon Noi of Ligor to invade the Kedah Sultanate in 1821'; infobox 12 November 1821; 'Siam imposed the direct rule through Ligor and installed Siamese personnel in Kedah, thus the sultanate ceased to exist for a time.' Sultan Ahmad Tajuddin fled to Penang. Matches the Rattanakosin dossier's 1821 gain.

region.text: Kedah proper, without Perlis: 'In 1842, the Sultan agreed to accept Siamese terms and was restored to the throne of Kedah'; Siam then made Perlis a separate principality, a direct vassal of Bangkok (the page, paraphrased)

ledger.note: 1842: the sultan is restored under Siamese suzerainty, without Perlis. The Siamese invasion page: Kedah 'was eventually restored to the Kedah Sultanate in 1842 under Siamese suzerainty', after Tengku Kudin's recapture of Alor Setar in 1831 and the Burney Treaty of 26 June 1826. The Perlis page ties Perlis's separation to 1839 ('the death of Siam's Ligor governor in 1839') and Sayyid Hussain Jamalullail's appointment to 1843; Kubang Pasu and Setul were separate states. Matches the Rattanakosin dossier's 1842 loss and vassal_start.

1892: Setul is reunified with Kedah. 'In 1892, the kingdom was reunified with the Kedah Sultanate.' The page does not name the kingdom in the text read; Setul is meant by context. Setul is read as Satun province.

region.text: one grid cell on the Perak border (100.62E 5.18N)

ledger.note: c. 1895: Cliopatria's shape gains one cell on its southern border from the British (it was Perak's in 1842-1876 and the British Colonial Empire's to 1894). No page opened mentions it.

region.text: Setul: the treaty 'finally ended Kedahan rule over Setul, as the Siamese and British agreed to exclude Setul from Kedah's jurisdiction'

ledger.note: 1909: Setul is excluded from Kedah by the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 9 July 1909 and stays with Siam (the Perlis page: 'Satun remained with Thailand').

region.text: Kedah, passing from Siamese suzerainty to a British protectorate

ledger.note: 1909: Kedah becomes a British protectorate. 'It was originally an independent state, but became a British protectorate in 1909'; infobox 'Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909: 9 July 1909' and 'Protectorate of the United Kingdom (1909-1941; 1945-1946)'. The Rattanakosin dossier ends Siam's suzerainty over Kedah in July 1909. The sultan remained, so the Cliopatria row's 1910 end is read as the same event.

wars.name: Aceh's attack on Kedah
wars.outcome: Sultan Sulaiman Shah was captured by Aceh in 1619; no territory is recorded as changing hands.
wars.note: 'Sulaiman Shah, who was captured by Aceh in 1619.' The Kedah page adds only that in the 17th century Kedah 'was attacked by the Portuguese after their conquest of Malacca, and by Aceh', without dates.

wars.name: Kedah-East India Company conflict over Penang

zones.text: Penang Island, which the Sultan planned to retake

wars.outcome: The British held Penang; Kedah's 1791 army in Seberang Perai was beaten and a ceasefire signed in 1791; the 1800 treaty added Seberang Perai.
wars.note: 'In 1790, Abdullah planned to launch an amphibious invasion of the island of Penang to recapture it'; 'The Sultan signed a ceasefire agreement with Light in 1791'; the Penang page: 'the Kedah Sultan in 1791 assembled an army in what is now Seberang Perai to retake the Prince of Wales Island'.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Kedah and Kedahan resistance

zones.text: Kedah proper, annexed in 1821 and restored in 1842

wars.outcome: Siam annexed Kedah in November 1821 and ruled it through Ligor; Tengku Kudin retook Alor Setar briefly in 1831 and another resistance came in 1838; the sultan was restored in 1842 under Siamese suzerainty.
wars.note: 'The Burney Treaty was concluded between Siam and British Empire on 26 June 1826.' The page does not describe the division of Kedah into Perlis, Kubang Pasu, Setul and Kedah proper.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the shapes are approximate cell outlines.
The border with Province Wellesley on the Perai River is sharp from 1800 ('turned the river into the international border'); the rest stays soft.
Kedah annexed by Siam; the sultan in exile in Penang; no Kedah territory of its own.
The partition lines with Perlis, Kubang Pasu and Setul are not described by any page opened.

notes: Page budget up to 5 pages, all five used (Kedah Sultanate twice). One state or successive states? The pages show one continuous sultanate, one dynasty, from the 1136 conversion to the British protectorate of 1909, with a break in territory (Siamese annexation 1821-1842) rather than in state; Cliopatria's row is therefore not split. A pre-1136 Kedah Kingdom (Hindu-Buddhist 'Kedah Tua') is the predecessor and needs its own dossier (not Cliopatria). The end is 1909 (July), not Cliopatria's 1910, and the sultanate persists as a British protectorate; the protectorate tint is Britain's to draw (eu-11). Not settled: (1) the 1294-1458 Satun-Songkhla strip has no page; (2) Kedah's overlords before 1821 (Majapahit's Nagarakretagama, Ayutthaya's bunga mas, Malacca's 15th-century overlordship, the Kedah page's 'conquered by the Malay sultanate of Malacca in the 15th century') are undated on the pages and belong to those states' ledgers; (3) the capital before the move to Alor Setar (Bukit Meriam in 1136, Kota Kuala Muda, Kota Star) is undated on the pages; (4) the 1895 and 1892 shapes: Setul (Satun) is an assumption for the territory of the Kingdom of Setul Mambang Segara; Langkawi is absent from the 1842-1910 Kedah shape and sits in Cliopatria's Kedah-Perlis District row; (5) the Kubang Pasu absorption into Kedah is undated ('absorbed into Kedah' on the Perlis page; Perlis page 1897: Kedah began efforts to end Perlis's sovereignty); (6) the 1896 combination of Kedah, Perlis and Setul into the Siamese province of Monthon Syburi is administrative and not drawn. States needing dossiers: kedah-kingdom, setul-mambang-segara (1808-1909), kubang-pasu (1839-?). No new gazetteer names needed (Setul is read as the Satun province; Langkawi would be a name to add if the gazetteer lacks it).
